questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: EU Institutions in the proximity and University with a good academic reputaiton

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although I came for the University and EU, I stayed for the people.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: KU Leuven makes it very easy, they take you by the hand. Just read your mails and attend the info sessions they hold.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A variety of info sessions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: KU Leuven owns a lot of different dorms in the city. The city is essentially one big campus due to its small size.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchen in the dorm i lived in (American College)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's great! Although you have to apply a good time in advance of your exchange so be aware of deadlines.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Intiutive IT system and info sessions that takes you through it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Info sessions and probably other things but i didn't need it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses i wanted. Non were cancelled and there was space for everyone on each course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to get pre-approval of as many courses as possible (only those you're interested in duh) because you will probably change your study-plan after your arrival. You have the oppertunity to attend all courses in the first weeks and I ended up changing after comparing teachers and tearching styles from those weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You didn't get a lot of feedback during semester so you didn't know how you were during. This can be frustrating in a new learning environment.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Similar to KU. More abstract as we're not applying concrete provisions of national law but more EU law and International law.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Only teaching in big lecture rooms (forelæsninger). No smaller groups (seminar undervisning). Although some courses have so few people registererd that it still can get the vibe of seminars.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Global Law (3 ECTS), European Social Security Law (3 ECTS), Law of International Organizations (6 ECTS), EU Constitutional Law (6 ECTS),  Social Policy and Law (6 ECTS), Global Environmental Politics (6 ECTS).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Global Law: Week intensive course during the semester (you don't have any other courses at the same time) in a topic you choose out of 20ish. This lightens the burden during exam season and its fun.

Social Policy and Law: Project exam during semester, so it also lightens the burden during exam season. 

Law of International Organization: Just personally super interesting:)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Using more money on eating out due to time constraint. That might you be a personal problem:)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarket were somewhat the same as in Denmark - had expected it to be a bit cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A broad range of sports, weekend trips, open mics and study help sessions.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sport! It's fun to play beach volley or padel with your new study buddies. In my opinion it brings you closer together than studying or bars will do. Salsa night at the Café Manger as it brings you closer to the local environment and its great fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Brussels (EU), Bruge (Beautiful), Ghent (Livly and Cultural) and Antwerpen (Livly and Cultural) are all obvious bun great!. 
You're in the heart of Europe so the train can take you to other capital cities in only a couple of hour.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy it's similar to copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Living in KU Leuven dorm helps as you meet them naturally there. There was enough to see to with the other exchange students so never really had the time.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friture and the students many events at FakBars (look them up). Also the architecture, which is very beautiful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. KU Leuven is renowned for being a tough uni, but it is also so very socially rich. So many cool event that makes the experience so worth it.
2. Leuven is small city (100.000 people - 60.000 are students) that almost gives it the energy of one big campus, which i personally loved. Other might find it too small. You're never more than 2 km away from where you need to be. I got a bike but a lot of people just walked everywhere.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember the law student association VRG. They consolidate the litterature for each course into books for a cheap price. Very handy. Also download quivr app for calendar, events, to see menu for the canteens and much more.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people for sure.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams. The level is somewhat the same as at UCPH, but the fact that it is written in hand makes it difficult. You don't have the time to erase or the space to add something you fotgot to add in the beginning. You will have to plan it out before writing essentially.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
